vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: workflow-builder-lite
Version: 1.6.1

The workflow-builder-lite skill is a logic-based tool for planning and simulating multi-step workflows within an agent session. It explicitly prohibits shell execution (exec steps), file persistence, and unauthorized data access, relying instead on the agent's built-in capabilities for API calls and task execution. No indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection attacks were found in SKILL.md or _meta.json.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches its stated purpose, but the instructions contain contradictory statements about file persistence and a few minor metadata inconsistencies; you should clarify before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (build and simulate session-only workflows) align with the instructions: no required binaries, no env vars, and execution limited to agent-built-in tools and HTTP calls. One mismatch: SKILL.md advertises a homepage URL while the registry entry lists none.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The document repeatedly claims "Workflows are session-only — they are never written to files or persisted," but an example interaction includes 'lagre resultat til fil' (save result to file). This is a direct contradiction about whether the agent will write files. The skill also states it will 'execute' approved workflows using built-in HTTP/agent tools (which implies network calls) while asserting 'Exec steps are simulation-only' (this latter point prevents shell execution but not external API/network calls). The agent is permitted to call external APIs — expected for this purpose but worth explicit confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — lowest-risk install surface. The SKILL.md shows a 'clawhub install' example but that is just user guidance, not an embedded installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested in the registry or the instructions. The skill does reference using built-in HTTP capabilities and other skills (smart-api-connector, cron tool), which implies network access but does not request extra secrets — proportional to its purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill claims session-only workflows and no persistence (which limits privilege), but the contradictory example that saves a file raises doubt about whether persistence may happen in practice. always:false and no special privileges are declared.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (plan and simulate workflows) and doesn't request credentials or install code, but there are small inconsistencies you should clarify before trusting it: 1) Confirm the persistence model — SKILL.md repeatedly states workflows are never written or persisted, yet an example shows saving results to a file; ask the author whether the agent can ever create files. 2) Confirm what "execute" means in practice: the skill will call external HTTP APIs (network calls) but not run shell commands — ensure you are comfortable with the agent making outgoing requests. 3) Verify the author/homepage (SKILL.md lists a homepage but the registry shows none) if provenance matters. If you need stronger assurances, request explicit guarantees that no file I/O or credential capture occurs and test the skill in a restricted environment first.
